compute.billingBasis: Hourly MCU accounting. One MCU bundles 1 vCPU-hour + 4 GB RAM-hours + 16 GB disk-hours, or 5 TB of snapshot-hours. For a Devbox the hourly MCU count is max(vCPUs, ceil(RAM/4GiB), ceil(disk/16GiB)), so the largest dimension sets the price rather than the dimensions adding up.

floor.detail: max(1, vCPUs, ceil(memory_MiB/4096), ceil(disk_size_MiB/16384)) for supported instances

increment.detail: The terms say per-second compute; the MCU is an hourly rate applied proportionally.
increment.quote: Per-second compute; per-operation Snapshot / Instance charges; snapshot / lineage storage (GB-hour); egress.

perResourceRates.quote: Based on standard MCU rate of $0.05

perResourceRates.notes: Equivalent rate when vCPU is the binding dimension.
Equivalent rate when RAM is the binding dimension. 4 GB per MCU at $0.05 means $0.0125 per GB-hour.
Disk is not a separate line item while running: it raises the MCU count once it exceeds 16 GiB per billed MCU.
5 TB (5,000 GB) hours per $0.05 MCU, i.e. $0.00001 per GB-hour, about $0.0073 per GB-month.

compute.notes: No fixed size list is published: vCPUs, memory and disk are chosen per snapshot/instance. Per-instance maximums and GPU availability are not published. CPU is billed on allocated vCPUs, not measured utilisation.

disk.detail: Root disk has no separate price while the instance runs; it enters the MCU formula at 16 GiB per MCU.
disk.quote: Decreasing disk capacity may leave the rate unchanged when CPU or memory already determines the maximum

billedWhileStopped.model: paused instance is replaced by a snapshot; only snapshot storage bills
billedWhileStopped.quote: You only get charged for the snapshot taken
billedWhileStopped.termsQuote: Paused instances incur only snapshot / storage charges.

snapshotStorage.detail: Derived from the published 5 TB snapshot-hours per $0.05 MCU; Morph does not print a snapshot dollar rate.

volumes.type: S3-compatible object storage, not an attached block disk

retention.stoppedDataKept: Snapshots have no default expiry; they persist until deleted or until an optional TTL expires. Retention of the implicit snapshot created by pausing is not published.
retention.quote: When you set `ttl_seconds`, it must be greater than zero.
retention.notes: Stopping (rather than pausing) releases the instance; the docs say a stopped instance's running state is lost and you start again from a snapshot.

egress.quote: Typical components may include but are not limited to compute, snapshot storage, and egress.
egress.notes: Egress is named as a billable component in the terms but no per-GB rate or free allowance is published on the pricing page or docs.

diffs.ours: The MCU formula has a floor of 1, so even a tiny instance bills one MCU per hour.
diffs.battleships: Its shorthand MCU formula is written without the max(1, ...) term, but its on-demand mode separately sets min_vcpu: 1, so no supported workload is shown to bill below one MCU. Not a demonstrated floor undercharge; its separate disk-dominated limitation (disk above 16 GiB per billed MCU) is real.

diffs.ours: Snapshot retention after pause was not published.

manualRoute: Create a Devbox from a template or snapshot in the dashboard, or call the Python/TypeScript SDK or CLI.
Install the agent inside the VM over SSH, the browser terminal, or an exec call.
Expose the agent's port as an HTTP service if it needs a URL, and enable wake-on-HTTP and wake-on-SSH.
Set a TTL with ttl_action=pause plus wake-on so the VM pauses instead of running forever.

evidence.claim: The dashboard can start a Devbox from a template and open it in an editor.
evidence.quote: Create a devbox from a template (or a snapshot)

evidence.claim: Interactive access includes SSH and the Devbox API.
evidence.quote: through SSH, or puppeteered through the Devbox API

evidence.claim: Idle shutdown is a TTL plus wake-on pattern, not a built-in agent supervisor.

deploy.notes: No Hermes or OpenClaw guide, template or one-click deploy was found anywhere in Morph's documentation index. A non-coder can start a template Devbox from the dashboard, but installing and keeping an agent alive still needs a shell and lifecycle configuration. Morph does publish a Claude Code example, which is the closest official agent walkthrough.
